commodities.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
commodities.context: Rebounded from $83.85 trough on April 17 after re-closure reports emerged; down 34% from $128 peak on April 2
commodities.commentary: WTI crude rebounded to $86.25/bbl on April 20 after reports of potential Strait of Hormuz re-closure reversed the post-ceasefire decline.1 The benchmark collapsed from approximately $128/bbl on April 2 to $83.85 on April 17 — a 34% decline in 15 days — following the April 8 ceasefire and April 17 Strait reopening.1 EIA scenario analysis projects $110/bbl under a 1-quarter outage and $132/bbl under a 2-quarter disruption.2 The pipeline tracks 39 oil and gas projects valued at $97.3B with direct WTI exposure.3

commodities.name: Crude Oil (Brent)
commodities.context: Wider Brent-WTI spread reflects seaborne supply risk premium; OPEC+ output fell 9.4 mb/d
commodities.commentary: Brent crude traded at $95.42/bbl, maintaining an elevated spread over WTI as seaborne supply risk remained priced in.1 OPEC+ production fell 9.4 mb/d month-over-month to 42.4 mb/d during the blockade period.2 Approximately 25% of seaborne oil and 20% of global LNG transited the Strait of Hormuz prior to disruption.1 Canada's TMX pipeline provides an alternative corridor for Asian buyers, supporting the strategic rationale for tracked energy export infrastructure.3

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.context: Henry Hub supported by LNG disruption premium and spring storage concerns
commodities.commentary: Henry Hub natural gas traded at $2.71/MMBtu, supported by Hormuz-related LNG supply disruption and below-average spring storage injections.1 The Strait's closure removed approximately 20% of global LNG transit capacity, tightening Atlantic Basin pricing.2 LNG Canada Phase 1 (Kitimat) and tracked BC natural gas projects have exposure to the global LNG rebalancing.3

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.context: Near record on geopolitical risk and central bank demand; Goldman Sachs Dec 2026 target $4,900
commodities.commentary: Gold traded near $4,828/oz, up +9.09% over the past month and +40.03% year-over-year as Hormuz uncertainty, global rate-hike repricing, and central bank reserve diversification sustained demand.4 Goldman Sachs maintained a December 2026 target of $4,900/oz.4 The pipeline tracks 305 mining projects valued at $146.0B, including gold operations in Ontario, Quebec, and British Columbia that benefit from elevated pricing.3

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.context: Industrial and monetary demand both elevated; gold-silver ratio near 153:1
commodities.commentary: Silver traded at approximately $31.45/oz, gaining alongside gold while also supported by industrial demand from solar panel manufacturing and electronics.4

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.context: China industrial production +6.1% supporting demand; electrification buildout continues
commodities.commentary: Copper traded at approximately $4.52/lb, supported by China's industrial production growth of +6.1% in Q1 and sustained electrification demand globally.5 Canadian copper mining operations, including tracked BC and Ontario projects, have exposure to the U.S. Section 232 tariff of 50% on copper imports.6

commodities.name: Aluminum
commodities.context: U.S. 50% Section 232 tariff on aluminum reshaping North American trade flows
commodities.commentary: Aluminum traded near $1.18/lb. U.S. Section 232 duties restructured to 50% on aluminum affect Canadian smelters in Quebec and BC that export to U.S. markets.6 Canada's retaliatory tariff pause (April 15) provides a 6-month window for negotiation.6

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.context: Housing starts at 235,852 SAAR below consensus; building permits -8.4%
commodities.commentary: Lumber traded near $520/mfbm, pressured by Canadian housing starts of 235,852 SAAR (-6.0% M/M) and building permits declining -8.4% to $12.1B.7 The 166 tracked residential projects ($31.9B) face a structural gap between current starts and CMHC's 430,000-480,000 annual target for affordability.3

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien)
commodities.context: Global supply stable; Saskatchewan production steady; spring planting season demand
commodities.commentary: Potash traded near $310/MT with Saskatchewan production — which accounts for approximately 30% of global supply — operating at steady rates through spring planting season demand.8

commodities.name: Uranium
commodities.context: Energy security narrative strengthened by Hormuz crisis; nuclear renaissance demand
commodities.commentary: Uranium spot traded near $68.50/lb, supported by energy security concerns amplified by the Hormuz crisis and continued nuclear capacity commitments globally.2 Saskatchewan's Cameco operations and tracked uranium projects benefit from the structural supply deficit narrative.3

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.context: Spring planting underway in Western Canada; global supply concerns from Black Sea disruptions
commodities.commentary: Canadian wheat traded near C$8.15/bu as spring planting commenced across the Prairies. Global supply concerns and elevated input costs supported pricing.8

commodities.name: Iron Ore
commodities.context: China March imports +27.8% YoY; industrial production +6.1% supporting steel demand
commodities.commentary: Iron ore traded near $105/MT, supported by China's March imports surging +27.8% year-over-year — the strongest growth since November 2021.5 Tracked Labrador and Quebec iron ore projects have direct exposure to Chinese steel demand.3

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.context: EV battery demand growing; Indonesian supply overhang persists
commodities.commentary: Nickel traded near $7.25/lb, with EV battery demand providing a floor against Indonesian supply expansion.5 Tracked Ontario and Labrador nickel projects maintain exposure to the energy transition supply chain.3

commodity_commentary:
Commodity markets this week remained dominated by Strait of Hormuz developments and their cascading effects across the energy complex. WTI crude's 34% collapse from its April 2 peak of approximately $128/bbl to the April 17 trough of $83.85 represented the most violent price swing since March 2020, before re-closure reports drove a rebound to $86.25.1 The Brent-WTI spread widened as seaborne supply risk commanded a premium, with OPEC+ production declining 9.4 mb/d during the blockade period.2

Precious metals sustained gains with gold near $4,828/oz — up +40% year-over-year — reflecting geopolitical hedging and central bank reserve diversification.4 Base metals advanced on China's stronger-than-expected Q1 GDP of +5.0% and industrial production growth of +6.1%.5 Iron ore benefited from China's March imports surging +27.8% year-over-year.5

Construction-linked commodities presented a mixed picture: lumber remained soft as Canadian building permits fell -8.4% and housing starts missed consensus, while copper held firm on electrification demand despite U.S. 50% Section 232 tariffs on imports.67 The pipeline's 550 power and energy projects, 305 mining projects, and 39 oil and gas projects — collectively valued at $734.2B — carry direct commodity price exposure to these movements.3
wcs_analysis: Western Canadian Select traded at an estimated discount of $12-14/bbl below WTI, narrower than the $15-18 range observed during peak Hormuz disruption as TMX operational capacity provided an alternative egress route to Asian markets.1 The narrowing differential supports economics for 39 tracked oil sands projects with breakeven costs concentrated above $65/bbl WTI.3
